confirmed.title: Infinity
confirmed.verbatim: OLAMIDE FT OMAH LAY | INFINITY | Award Silver | Format Single | Corporate Group/Label YBNL NATION | Latest Certification 07.08.2026 | Released 09.10.2020 — permalink detail: "Single | OLAMIDE FT OMAH LAY | INFINITY | Most Recent Certification Silver | Release Date 09 October 2020 | Corporate Group/Label YBNL NATION | Most Recent Certification Date 07 August 2026 | Certification history: 07 August 2026 Silver"

verdict.reasoning:
Attempted refutation at the body's own live register (certified-awards.bpi.co.uk, the htmx app; bpi.co.uk/brit-certified/ is dead) and could not refute it. Confirmed three independent ways: (1) artist-side search "OLAMIDE" returns exactly two rows, one being OLAMIDE FT OMAH LAY | INFINITY | Silver | Single | YBNL NATION | 07.08.2026 | Released 09.10.2020; (2) the detail permalink /format/2/artist/6924/title/10277 returns character-for-character the claimed detail, with certification history showing a single step "07 August 2026 Silver"; (3) cross-check via artist-side "OMAH LAY" surfaces the same artist-id-6924 row alongside his three own-credit rows.

The collision risk was real and the claim survives it. A title-side sweep for INFINITY returns 13 rows, and four distinct singles share title id 10277: JAYMES YOUNG (artist 5108, Gold), ONE DIRECTION (artist 1996, Silver), GURU JOSH PROJECT (artist 2003, Platinum) and OLAMIDE FT OMAH LAY (artist 6924, Silver). The register disambiguates only by artist id, so a title-only match could have imported Guru Josh's Platinum. The claimed row is pinned to artist 6924, whose credit string is exclusively "OLAMIDE FT OMAH LAY" — Olamide is the printed LEAD credit, not an inferred feature — and the label is YBNL Nation, his own imprint. Matches the real record: "Infinity" (Olamide feat. Omah Lay) from Carpe Diem, Oct 2020.

Format is Single, confirmed structurally rather than by label alone: across the 13-row title sweep every format/2 row renders "Single" and every format/3 row renders "Album". Multiplier is correctly absent — the certification history is one step with no Gold or Platinum above it, and BPI publishes each tier as its own dated award, so this is 1 plaque at Silver (200,000 units).

Incidental: the same 07.08.2026 batch also produced ASAKE FT OLAMIDE | AMAPIANO | Silver | Single, so Olamide's BPI total is 2, both Silver singles as a credited collaborator on YBNL Nation. Note also that docs/sweeps/omah-lay-certifications-v1.md already carries this same Infinity Silver on Omah Lay's side — correct to count per-artist for both, but it must not be double-counted in any cross-artist total.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at the body's own register. The BPI database now lives at https://certified-awards.bpi.co.uk/ (iframed into bpi.co.uk/page/certified-awards after the site moved to Hivebrite). Searching "Amapiano" returns exactly ONE row in the entire register: "ASAKE FT OLAMIDE | AMAPIANO | Award Silver | Format Single | Corporate Group/Label YBNL NATION | Latest Certification 07.08.2026 | Released 23.05.2023". Opening the register's own permalink (/format/2/artist/6925/title/22152) gives the detail page: Single, ASAKE FT OLAMIDE, AMAPIANO, Most Recent Certification Silver, Release Date 23 May 2023, Label YBNL NATION, Most Recent Certification Date 07 August 2026, Certification history: 07 August 2026 Silver (one entry only). (1) Row exists at Silver: confirmed. (2) Credit: printed literally as "ASAKE FT OLAMIDE" — Olamide is named as featured artist, so attribution to him is legitimate. Same-title collision is ruled out because "Amapiano" yields exactly one row register-wide, and the label (YBNL NATION, Olamide's own imprint) and 23 May 2023 release date match the genuine Asake/Olamide single. (3) Format Single is correct; the permalink's /format/2/ is the register's Single code (Album rows use /format/3/). (4) Multiplier correct — Silver takes no multiplier and the certification history shows a single award with no prior or stacked entries. Cross-check: searching "Olamide" returns exactly two rows, both Silver singles on YBNL NATION certified 07.08.2026 ("Infinity" by OLAMIDE FT OMAH LAY, and this "Amapiano"), consistent with one batch of YBNL certs landing that day. Could not refute on any of the four checks; every reported field matches the register verbatim.

Omah Lay | Forever (Remix) | Platinum | 2022-07-28'. Black Sherif's distributor EMPIRE has 18 rows in the register, none his. Tier vocabulary confirmed: Gold (379) / Platinum (203) / Double-Platinum (77) / Multi-Platinum (86) — NO Diamond tier and no numeric multiplier above 2x, as the brief says. Tier is encoded only in the award image filename (certified-streaming-awards-gold | -platinum | -dbl-plat | -multi-plat).

Ghana — NO CERTIFICATION REGISTER EXISTS TO SWEEP. This is a structural finding, established positively rather than by failure to load a page, and it resolves the question the previous session left UNRESOLVED. Four independent lines: (1) IFPI's own Local Associations directory (https://www.ifpi.org/about-us/local-associations/, read in full) lists exactly THREE African entries — Kenya (RIKE), Nigeria (ReLPI) and South Africa (RiSA). Ghana is absent. (2) GHAMRO's LIVE site is not the dead ghamro.org host the previous session hit; it is https://www.ghamroonline.org/ , which loads fine and which I read in full. Its stated mandate is 'To license music users, collect, and distribute music royalties to music right holders (Copyright Regulation L.I 1962, Copyright Amendment Regulation L.I 2469)' — a collecting society. The words certification / certified / platinum / plaque appear ZERO times anywhere on it, and it has no awards or certification route. (3) The dead ghamro.org host was crawled through the Wayback CDX index in full — 666 unique URLs, captures 2013→2020 only — and grepping every path for cert|gold|platin|plaque|award|sales|chart yields exactly two hits, an images/certificate.jpg and an images/pdf/CHARTS.pdf, neither a certification register. (4) Ghana appears in NEITHER standard reference table: Wikipedia's 'List of music recording certifications' names only Egypt, Nigeria (TCSN) and South Africa (RiSA) for Africa, and 'Music recording certification' names only RiSA and TCSN under Africa. The Telecel Ghana Music Awards (ghanamusicawards.com, fetched — no certification vocabulary) and the 3Music Awards are annual awards ceremonies, not sales/streaming certification programmes. TurnTable's scheme is explicitly the TurnTable Certification System OF NIGERIA and has no Ghanaian counterpart. Black Sherif's only African register plaques are therefore his Nigerian TCSN ones, which this project already holds (24 titles).

RIKE / Recording Industry of Kenya — NO CERTIFICATION REGISTER. Kenya IS one of only three African IFPI local associations, so it was worth checking properly. rike.or.ke read in full: its published objectives cover 'Establishment of local chart in accordance with globally aligned practices', an ISRC register, anti-piracy and advocacy — a chart body and CMO-adjacent trade association, with no gold/platinum programme. /certification and /certifications both 404; the about page and membership subdomain carry no certification programme. Nothing to sweep, and nothing for either artist.
gaps: ARIA (AU) — GAP, not a zero. ARIA publishes no searchable certification register. Its only public list of awarded titles is https://www.aria.com.au/latest-accreditations, which is a static page whose own header reads "Current as of 31 August 2020". I read that page in full: 353 data rows (Artist / Title / Co. / Accreditation), containing no Olamide and no Black Sherif — but the only Afrobeats entries in it are 'Jorja Smith Feat. Burna Boy — Be Honest — ORCH — GOLD' and 'Stormzy Feat. Ed Sheeran & Burna Boy — Own It — WAR — GOLD', and the cutoff predates every release at issue (Olamide's 'Infinity' released 09.10.2020; 'Amapiano' 2023; Black Sherif's entire career from 2021). https://www.aria.com.au/accreditations is explanatory only (thresholds and application PDFs, no awarded titles); ARIA chart pages carry no accreditation badges; the sitemap exposes no other accreditation route; /charts/accreditations and /industry/accreditations both 404. Post-August-2020 ARIA accreditations are published only in the member-gated ARIA Report. Absence from the 2020 snapshot is therefore not evidence either artist is uncertified in Australia.

Ultratop (Belgium) — could not be read, so this is a gap and NOT a zero. Every path on ultratop.be except /robots.txt returns Cloudflare HTTP 403 to curl (tried https/http, www and bare host, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, full Chrome header sets, both the /fr/or-platine/<year>/ and /nl/goud-platina/<year>/ sides) and also to WebFetch. In a real browser the page sits permanently on the Cloudflare 'Performing security verification' interstitial and never clears, across ~90s of waiting and repeated reloads in two fresh tabs. Ultratop's own robots.txt carries an explicit 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: /', so this is a deliberate operator opt-out and I did not attempt to work around the challenge. The usual fallback — Wayback captures of the award-year pages — was also unavailable: web.archive.org served 429 and then an 'Internet Archive services are temporarily offline' page for the whole session, and the CDX API never responded. No Belgian conclusion should be drawn either way until Ultratop or the Internet Archive is reachable again.

GLF / Sverigetopplistan (SE) — GAP, not a zero. The actual Swedish register is Grammotex and its RECORD endpoint is public over http:// (I re-verified it live: sart=9225432 renders 'Artist: BURNA BOY / Titel: GBONA / Guld/Platina: Guld - cert.nr 10453 - 2023-08-16'), but its SEARCH is login-walled (grammotex.se/catalogue.php posts login/losen to sys2.grammotex.se/netcomm/base000.mbr), and record ids are assigned in ingestion order so they cannot be enumerated. IFPI Sverige's own page /musikbolag/guld-och-platina/ publishes thresholds and rules ONLY, no list of awarded titles, and routes applications to sys.ifpi.se, which is unreachable from here (members-only). Sverigetopplistan's public search DOES print Guld/Platina badges and returns 0 hits for Olamide, Black Sherif, Blacko and Sherif — but it is demonstrably NOT a complete certification register and must not be read as one: Burna Boy's 11 rows there carry badges for Love, Damini (Guld), Last Last (Platina) and For My Hand (Platina), yet omit Gbona, Ye, African Giant and On the Low, all four of which ARE Swedish-certified per Grammotex cert nos 10448/10450/10452/10453. A Swedish plaque on a title that never charted is invisible on that surface, so its silence proves nothing.

CNS IFPI — Czechia (CZ) — GAP. /oceneni publishes award RULES only (six criteria PDFs for CR and SR), with no register of awarded titles anywhere on the site. The only certification surface is the tier printed inside a currently-charting row. I read chartId 30 (CZ - SINGLES DIGITAL - TOP 100), week 34/2026, IN FULL — 100 rows, 39 certification badges parsed — and neither artist appears; positive control in that same read: 'Zlaty singl' on shakira-burna-boy / dai-dai (id 180018). But one week is not the register. The weekly archive exists (weekIds 1296 = wk1 2006 through 3029 = wk34 2026) and is NOT reachable: a GET with ?weekId= is ignored and returns the current week, and the Nette POST contract (_do=chart-chartForm-submit + chartId + weekId) could not be completed because the host began refusing TCP connections mid-sweep (connect time 0.000000, ECONNREFUSED on 62.109.154.161:443) and had not recovered after a 90s backoff, three retries and a UA change; the /front.charts/download?chartId=&weekId= export also timed out. Wayback holds ZERO captures of ifpicr.cz/hitparada/30. Neither artist can be cleared historically.

CNS IFPI — Slovakia (SK) — GAP, and weaker than Czechia: I could not read it AT ALL. chartId 43 (SK - SINGLES DIGITAL - TOP 100) and 36 (SK - ALBUMS) were never retrieved — every attempt hit the same ECONNREFUSED that closed out the Czech pass. Wayback holds zero captures of ifpicr.cz/hitparada/43. No Slovak row of any kind was read, so nothing about Slovakia may be reported as a zero.

IFPI Greece — PARTIAL, not a zero. Greece publishes certifications only as an unlabelled Award column inside the weekly international digital singles chart at ifpi.gr/digital_ien.html, overwritten every week, so the register only exists as a snapshot series. Read: the live page plus 423 readable Wayback captures covering 310 distinct chart weeks (2018-W12 -> 2026), of which 198 weeks carry the Award column (2021: 45/52, 2022: 47/52, 2023: 44/52, 2024: 35/52, 2025: 22/52, 2026: 5/34). Roughly 96 award-bearing weeks — concentrated in 2024-2026 — were never captured or could not be retrieved, so they are unreadable rather than empty. Zero rows for either artist in every week read; neither has ever charted in Greece at all, and Greece badges only currently-charting titles. Two structural limits on top of that: the Award column did not exist before 2021, and no Greek page carries album certifications in any capture, so Greek album plaques are unreadable by construction. Sandbox note for any re-run: port 80 is blocked here, so the project's documented http:// Wayback recipe fails silently — use https://web.archive.org/web/{ts}id_/... with --compressed, and expect archive.org to throttle hard (~2-5 captures/minute).

AFP / Audiogest (Portugal) — PARTIAL, not a zero. There is no standalone register; awards appear as the Gal. column (OU / PL…9PL) on the TOP AFP/AUDIOGEST reports. Read: all 8 published annual reports (2017-2024) plus 206 weekly PDFs spanning 2021-01-21 to 2026-08-26, 218,649 indexed rows. Zero awards for either artist. Three gaps remain and none can be closed from the published PDFs. (1) Annual depth varies enormously — 2022 is 10,000 positions deep but 2021 reaches only ~1,154 unique titles, 2023 ~410 and 2024 ~702, so a deep-catalogue award in those years is invisible. (2) The TOP Anual 2025 and TOP Anual 2026 links on audiogest.pt/tabelas-oficiais-de-vendas-?lang=pt are still href="#" — unpublished. (3) Awards to titles that were NOT charting when the plaque landed appear only in Audiogest's monthly award cards on facebook.com/audiogest and instagram.com/audiogest; facebook.com/audiogest/ returns HTTP 400 to a logged-out client, and no login was attempted, so that channel is gated. audiogest.pt/noticias carries no award tables.

Egypt — GAP, never a zero. Wikipedia's 'List of music recording certifications' names 'International Federation of the Phonographic Industry – Egypt' as the Egyptian certifying body, and a threshold set has existed since ~2005, but Egypt is NOT in IFPI's Local Associations directory (its only Egyptian IFPI entries are the record companies Alam El Phan and Mazzika Group, i.e. corporate members, not a national group). No Egyptian certification register was located or read — no host, endpoint or published list. IFPI does now run MENA charts covering Egypt, but a chart is not a certification register. Egypt is unread, so nothing about either artist can be concluded from it.

MUSIGA (Musicians Union of Ghana) — content not read. musiga.org.gh has no DNS record at all; www.musiga.org resolves (198.251.83.50) but every request is intercepted by a cPGuard 'human verification' wall which I did not attempt to bypass. This does not weaken the Ghana finding — MUSIGA is a musicians' trade union, not a certifying body, and Ghana's absence from IFPI's association list and from both reference tables is established independently — but its own pages were not read.

African territories not individually queried — Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Uganda, Senegal, Cameroon, Ivory Coast, Ethiopia and the rest. None appears in IFPI's Local Associations directory and none is named as a certifying territory in either standard reference table, so there is no positive evidence any of them runs a register; but I did not query each body's own site, so this is an absence of evidence, not a swept zero.

RiSA window after 2026-07-14 — the live register's newest row is dated 14 Jul 2026, about six weeks before today. Anything RiSA has certified since then is not yet published and was not read. The zero for both artists is proven through 2026-07-14.
